quick.summary: How to edit a data model without breaking the dashboards everyone uses.
quick.takeaway: Build a draft copy, check the numbers, and ask for a review.

beats.line: I added a column and broke the finance board. How do I stop that?
Think of a restaurant kitchen. You would not invent a new soup during dinner.
Right. I would test it in the morning.
Exactly. For data, you make your changes in a safe space.
We call this making a feature branch.
Can I just say making a draft copy?
Yes. A draft only you can see.
You build the draft. You check the numbers. Then you ask.
Ask a teammate to review my draft before it goes live.
Yes. Two sets of eyes are safer.

quiz.question: Why should you build a draft copy of your data model first?
options: To keep bad changes away from the main dashboard.
To make the system run your math faster.
To avoid paying for extra server time.
To bypass the review process entirely.
quiz.explanation: A draft gives you a safe space to test changes without impacting everyone else.

quiz.question: Asking a teammate to review your changes is unnecessary if the numbers look right.
quiz.explanation: Even if things look correct to you, two sets of eyes catch problems you might miss.
